primary_meaning: In Christian teaching, 'elders' most commonly carry the symbolic meaning of the representative leadership of God's covenant people — mature, authoritative figures who stand for and govern the whole community. When the term is treated symbolically (most notably the twenty-four elders of Revelation 4–5), the dominant interpretation is that they represent the totality of the redeemed people of God across both covenants: the twelve tribes of Israel plus the twelve apostles (12 + 12 = 24), depicted as enthroned, crowned, and worshiping — i.e., the church/people of God glorified and reigning with God.
primary_basis: Revelation 21:12-14 (twelve tribes' gates plus twelve apostles' foundations, supporting the 12+12 reading)
Exodus 24:1, 9-11 (seventy elders ascend and behold God, prototype of elders in the divine presence)
Numbers 11:16-25 (seventy elders share Moses' spirit and authority)
Acts 14:23; Acts 15:2-6; Acts 20:17, 28 (elders as appointed representative leaders of the churches)
1 Peter 5:1-4 (elders shepherd the flock and receive the crown of glory)
James 5:14 (elders act on behalf of the congregation)
Isaiah 24:23 (the LORD reigns 'before his elders' in glory)

alternatives.meaning: The twenty-four elders of Revelation are angelic beings — members of the heavenly court or divine council — not redeemed humans. Advocates note they are distinguished from the redeemed in Revelation 5:8-10 (in some manuscript readings they sing about the redeemed rather than as them) and that they function like the heavenly council of 1 Kings 22:19 and Isaiah 24:23.
basis: Revelation 7:13-14 (an elder speaks as an informant distinct from the saved multitude)

alternatives.meaning: The twenty-four elders represent specifically the church raptured and rewarded in heaven before the tribulation (a classic dispensationalist reading), emphasizing their crowns as the believer's rewards already granted.
basis: Revelation 4:4 (crowns and white garments as promised rewards, cf. Revelation 2:10; 3:5, 11)

alternatives.meaning: The twenty-four elders correspond to the twenty-four priestly courses of the temple, symbolizing glorified priestly worship and service before God (sometimes combined with, sometimes distinct from, the 'whole people of God' view).
basis: Revelation 5:8 (elders with harps and bowls of incense, priestly imagery)

alternatives.meaning: The elders represent only Old Testament saints or only the apostles/church (one half of the 12+12 scheme rather than both), i.e., a narrower identification of which redeemed group is in view.

Non-symbolic/institutional reading: 'elders' is simply an office or social role (Israel's elders at the gate, synagogue elders, church presbyters) and carries no symbolic freight beyond ordinary leadership and wisdom of age.

notes: The term operates on two levels. (1) As an ordinary biblical office (Israel's elders, church presbyters), the meaning — representative, governing, shepherding leadership of God's people — is essentially uncontested and functions more as a role than a symbol. (2) As a symbol, the debate centers almost entirely on the twenty-four elders of Revelation. There the '12 tribes + 12 apostles = the whole redeemed people of God' reading is the most widely taught in churches and popular commentary, but modern critical scholarship contains a substantial and arguably comparable stream identifying them as angelic members of the heavenly council; dispensationalist circles favor the raptured-church reading; the priestly-courses reading is often blended into the majority view. Because the identity of the twenty-four elders remains genuinely disputed among reputable interpreters, I mark the symbolic consensus as unsettled, while noting that the 'redeemed people of God' interpretation is the single most recognizable answer in general Christian teaching.
